training: All six candidates and duplicate original control, fixed 16x7. Two training sources; warmup plus three randomized repetitions. No test source used to select.
selection: Candidate must improve both source medians at least 5%, beat both baseline and duplicate control geometric means by 5%, and use <=1.25x edge work on each training source. Select fastest eligible by geomean of source medians; fall back to original heap8.
heldout: Freeze queue and prior training-selected layout. Randomized base/queue/layout/combined/control/Wasp, four test sources, warmup plus three measured repetitions. This repeats layout comparison in a second allocation.
work: All six candidates on both training sources plus selected combined if layout differs; diagnostic time is not production timing. Verify publication/take and normal work ledgers.
predictions: Broader band65536 may fill more 64-entry chunks with road weights up to368855, at risk of extra relaxations from FIFO disorder.
At fixed band, owner-serviced partial publication may increase peer transfers and reduce idle/pop-probe cost, at risk of atomic and mutex overhead.
Heap slice64 is an independent low-overhead alternative to reduce scheduling without changing queue ordering.
Layout and queue may interact; only the frozen 2x2 confirmation supports combined benefit.
correctness: Unit tests, ASan/UBSan/TSan; full small-graph serial and Bellman-certificate gate with road-scale weights and source reuse; every large solve full independent digest, actual affinity, old scheduler. Abort on first invalid solve.
scope: One node at a time in cpu-interactive; queue is compile-time opt-in; no global or distributed default change.
